mwalimu/cb03a75e.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/cb03a75e.text: You're Amani. Good. I'm Chief Inspector Wairimu. Everyone here calls me Mwalimu, and you'll find out why.

mwalimu/069a30a0.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/069a30a0.text: A driver at Ngara stage. Read the OB, go to the scene, look at everything twice. I'll be on the phone if you need me.

mwalimu/4b12b722.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/4b12b722.text: Registers are kept by people who weren't thinking about murder. That's why they're honest. Read every row, not just the one you came for.

mwalimu/a0ba30c8.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/a0ba30c8.text: Times matter now. Your notebook has a Time tab: everyone you can place, lined up on one clock.

mwalimu/f43dab2f.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/f43dab2f.text: Two places today. Both are in the folder. Go back and forth as often as you like. Walking costs you nothing.

mwalimu/bddc454b.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/bddc454b.text: When two papers talk about the same thing, put them side by side. Pin a line from each in your notebook and read the Pinned tab.

mwalimu/34c26fc6.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/34c26fc6.text: A building, not a street. Before you decide who was where, ask how anyone got from one floor to another.

mwalimu/9e8c79ab.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/9e8c79ab.text: Open the Time tab. Every bar is someone you can place. The empty stretches deserve as much attention as the bars.

mwalimu/ab8b26c2.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/ab8b26c2.text: Small writing matters. Tap any photograph to open it full size, then pinch or double-tap to look closer.

mwalimu/0d52205a.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/0d52205a.text: Not everything that looks guilty is. When something points at a person, ask what else could explain it before you write a name.

mwalimu/b6baaa41.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/b6baaa41.text: A timetable says where a train should be. People tell you where they were. Hold one against the other.

mwalimu/5ae588ed.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/5ae588ed.text: Read every exhibit twice: once for what it shows, and once for what it ought to show.

mwalimu/7f2ed231.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/7f2ed231.text: This one takes three steps, not two. If your name rests on a single fact, you're not finished.

mwalimu/53256677.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/53256677.text: You can pin six facts. Keep the ones that belong together on the Pinned tab, and the board will show them too.

mwalimu/45769964.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/45769964.text: Photographs have backgrounds. Open it full size and look past the people in front.

mwalimu/60131cc2.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/60131cc2.text: Two blanks this time, judged together. Halima accepts both or neither, so be sure of each.

mwalimu/ec170671.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/ec170671.text: Everything you find lands here by itself. People, places, exhibits, and times. You don't write, you think.

mwalimu/b208531b.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/b208531b.text: The board is yours. Drag things where they make sense to you, tie string between them. Nobody grades it.

mwalimu/72c0d5d5.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/72c0d5d5.text: Call me when you're stuck. Where to look, what to notice, or the answer. Each one costs you a star you haven't earned yet, never the case.

mwalimu/ec32222d.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/ec32222d.text: The charge sheet. Only names you've actually found are in the bank. Halima reads every one.

mwalimu/daf43b7a.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/daf43b7a.text: Detective. You can call me. "Where to look" names the thing that matters. "What to notice" shows you two facts that belong together. "The answer" fills a blank, and costs you more.

c006-p_wycliffe/0cf1e98d.speaker: c006-p_wycliffe
c006-p_wycliffe/0cf1e98d.text: SIM trays? Every repair shop has a hundred.

c006-p_wycliffe/98a7f5de.speaker: c006-p_wycliffe
c006-p_wycliffe/98a7f5de.text: I came for my radio, it wasn't ready, I left. He was fine.

c006-p_wycliffe/0fba1d88.speaker: c006-p_wycliffe
c006-p_wycliffe/0fba1d88.text: I don't know anything about SIM trays.

c006-p_esther/ad04a69a.speaker: c006-p_esther
c006-p_esther/ad04a69a.text: He fixed my radio for free last year because my son had exams. He was that kind of man.

c007-p_grace/abe595ea.speaker: c007-p_grace
c007-p_grace/abe595ea.text: I only came back for carnations.

c007-p_grace/a01e4083.speaker: c007-p_grace
c007-p_grace/a01e4083.text: She gave me an extra rose for free and said, 'Next week, lilies, half price, tell your friends.'

c007-p_ahmed/0a749063.speaker: c007-p_ahmed
c007-p_ahmed/0a749063.text: Ask me. I see the whole aisle from here.

c007-p_ahmed/ea249a38.speaker: c007-p_ahmed
c007-p_ahmed/ea249a38.text: The lily lady? About five to twelve she walked back from Beatrice's side to her own stall, rubbing her hands on her apron like they were dirty.

c007-p_ahmed/140aa50f.speaker: c007-p_ahmed
c007-p_ahmed/140aa50f.text: The curio mama shouted at Beatrice this morning about buckets in the aisle. Then she went off with her fee book.

c007-p_ahmed/429a80d5.speaker: c007-p_ahmed
c007-p_ahmed/429a80d5.text: Kimani left early with his wedding flowers in a pickup. Half eleven, maybe.

c007-p_lucy/e7e17caa.speaker: c007-p_lucy
c007-p_lucy/e7e17caa.text: She brought in imported lilies at half my price. Half! Ten years I've sold lilies in this market.

c007-p_lucy/d8213fea.speaker: c007-p_lucy
c007-p_lucy/d8213fea.text: Everyone in this aisle has pollen on them. It's a flower market.

c007-p_lucy/6e639d30.speaker: c007-p_lucy
c007-p_lucy/6e639d30.text: I've been at my stall all morning. Ask anyone.

c007-p_lucy/e5a67e41.speaker: c007-p_lucy
c007-p_lucy/e5a67e41.text: Beatrice and I compete. That's the market. I didn't touch her.

c007-p_josphat/f637017c.speaker: c007-p_josphat
c007-p_josphat/f637017c.text: Forty dozen roses de-thorned since six this morning! Look at the boy's hands, look at mine. Call the cathedral.

c007-p_josphat/711b19fb.speaker: c007-p_josphat
c007-p_josphat/711b19fb.text: I was at the cathedral with the wedding flowers.

c007-p_naliaka/ffdd4ded.speaker: c007-p_naliaka
c007-p_naliaka/ffdd4ded.text: I know what Ahmed told you. Here.

c007-p_naliaka/5bd782e4.speaker: c007-p_naliaka
c007-p_naliaka/5bd782e4.text: We shouted about buckets. Every week we shout about buckets. It's the soko.

c007-p_naliaka/87416ac5.speaker: c007-p_naliaka
c007-p_naliaka/87416ac5.text: Yes, I shouted at her. Then I went to City Hall to pay my fees.

c008-p_felix/a61d2cf7.speaker: c008-p_felix
c008-p_felix/a61d2cf7.text: I found him. Me. And he called me a thief last month.

c008-p_felix/6cf9c6a7.speaker: c008-p_felix
c008-p_felix/6cf9c6a7.text: He said I stole soda crates. I didn't. But I'm the one who found him, so you'll look at me. Look at the parcels book.

c008-p_felix/3accba48.speaker: c008-p_felix
c008-p_felix/3accba48.text: Dorcas runs that kiosk more than he did. She catches the 18:10 every day. Every day.

c008-p_janet/7233a1ad.speaker: c008-p_janet
c008-p_janet/7233a1ad.text: I sell her the same ticket every day. I can tell you the exact minute.

c008-p_janet/2458e27f.speaker: c008-p_janet
c008-p_janet/2458e27f.text: Ten to six, 18:10 to Embakasi, like always. She looked upset. She usually jokes about the queue.

c008-p_janet/c2fd3aec.speaker: c008-p_janet
c008-p_janet/c2fd3aec.text: Mzee Elijah brought me tea at quarter to six. Then later I heard bottles crash, about five past. I thought he'd dropped a crate.

c008-p_musa/e8c93387.speaker: c008-p_musa
c008-p_musa/e8c93387.text: Twenty years on this line. I know my regulars.

c008-p_musa/901f62bd.speaker: c008-p_musa
c008-p_musa/901f62bd.text: Mama Dorcas? Every day she greets me, 'Musa, how is your back?' Not today. Not on my train.

c008-p_musa/2911b6a7.speaker: c008-p_musa
c008-p_musa/2911b6a7.text: No hole. Then it was never on my train. I punch every ticket before Makadara. Every one.

c008-p_dorcas/6b5d9351.speaker: c008-p_dorcas
c008-p_dorcas/6b5d9351.text: Elijah? I left him at the kiosk.

c008-p_dorcas/abbfb57a.speaker: c008-p_dorcas
c008-p_dorcas/abbfb57a.text: My name isn't on the licence because the county wanted one name. I put in half. Half! Five years.

c008-p_dorcas/cac9ab56.speaker: c008-p_dorcas
c008-p_dorcas/cac9ab56.text: I must have dropped it. I didn't take the train in the end. I took a matatu. I didn't feel like the crowd.

c008-p_dorcas/978bf229.speaker: c008-p_dorcas
c008-p_dorcas/978bf229.text: I bought my ticket and went home. I always go home on the 18:10.

c008-p_dorcas/420b828a.speaker: c008-p_dorcas
c008-p_dorcas/420b828a.text: Elijah and I were partners. I'd never hurt him.

c008-p_kamal/ed61134f.speaker: c008-p_kamal
c008-p_kamal/ed61134f.text: Elijah? He owed me, yes, but he always paid in the end.

c008-p_kamal/4c3e4dcb.speaker: c008-p_kamal
c008-p_kamal/4c3e4dcb.text: Three months of bread and milk. He said he'd sell and pay me. I'm sorry for him. I'm sorry for my money too, honestly.

c009-p_dennis/a5db1ae3.speaker: c009-p_dennis
c009-p_dennis/a5db1ae3.text: I was on the water. I was on the water and he was on the floor.

c009-p_dennis/7479bb72.speaker: c009-p_dennis
c009-p_dennis/7479bb72.text: His brother shouted at him at nine about their mother's shamba. Everyone heard. Then he left.

c009-p_dennis/66243e2f.speaker: c009-p_dennis
c009-p_dennis/66243e2f.text: The manager? He was around. In and out of the office. He does the count at four.

c009-p_dennis/0c285f27.speaker: c009-p_dennis
c009-p_dennis/0c285f27.text: I was rowing out for the boat that drifted. When I came back he was on the floor.

c009-p_pendo/e9cc9e3e.speaker: c009-p_pendo
c009-p_pendo/e9cc9e3e.text: Twenty years I've seen that shed. Twenty years.

c009-p_pendo/a2e57e88.speaker: c009-p_pendo
c009-p_pendo/a2e57e88.text: George came at nine, shouted, and stormed out with no cap, hands in the air. He never came back. I'd have seen him.

c009-p_pendo/9903d328.speaker: c009-p_pendo
c009-p_pendo/9903d328.text: Dennis was rowing for that drifting boat from ten to four. The children were cheering. He was on the water the whole time.

c009-p_pendo/b661a476.speaker: c009-p_pendo
c009-p_pendo/b661a476.text: The manager? He walks around a lot. I don't watch him. I watch the children near the water.

c009-p_victor/6260eb0a.speaker: c009-p_victor
c009-p_victor/6260eb0a.text: I write the time on every one. Customers like it. Police like it more.

c009-p_victor/d612da7b.speaker: c009-p_victor
c009-p_victor/d612da7b.text: Look in the background. Green overall. Only one man in this park wears that colour of overall.

c009-p_george/3ae89139.speaker: c009-p_george
c009-p_george/3ae89139.text: They're saying it was me. They're already saying it.

c009-p_george/53af7b0b.speaker: c009-p_george
c009-p_george/53af7b0b.text: My cap? I left it there in the morning. I was so angry I didn't notice. Mama Pendo saw me go.

c009-p_george/94c00b45.speaker: c009-p_george
c009-p_george/94c00b45.text: We fought about Mother's plot. He wanted to sell, I didn't. I'd give him the whole shamba to have him back.

c009-p_george/ff54af8d.speaker: c009-p_george
c009-p_george/ff54af8d.text: I shouted at him about our mother's shamba and I left. I was at Gikomba all day.

c009-p_daniel/577f0259.speaker: c009-p_daniel
c009-p_daniel/577f0259.text: Terrible. The brother was here this morning, you know.

c009-p_daniel/a2b6d97f.speaker: c009-p_daniel
c009-p_daniel/a2b6d97f.text: 'D'? Could be anyone. Dennis. Delivery men. Charles kept strange notes.

c009-p_daniel/194116f5.speaker: c009-p_daniel
c009-p_daniel/194116f5.text: Green overall? The owner sometimes wears one. Anyone can buy an overall.

c009-p_daniel/97d03f34.speaker: c009-p_daniel
c009-p_daniel/97d03f34.text: I was in the office doing the books all afternoon. I didn't hear anything.

c009-p_daniel/d01ee043.speaker: c009-p_daniel
c009-p_daniel/d01ee043.text: The brother was screaming at him this morning. Everyone heard.

c010-p_juma/f72b174b.speaker: c010-p_juma
c010-p_juma/f72b174b.text: He taught me to cut letters backwards. Backwards, so they print the right way.

c010-p_juma/9ae47366.speaker: c010-p_juma
c010-p_juma/9ae47366.text: He wrote down the ID of anyone who collected a stamp that looked official. Every time. He said a stamp is a promise.

c010-p_juma/b5d5fcc1.speaker: c010-p_juma
c010-p_juma/b5d5fcc1.text: Mvua. That job made him angry all week. He said, 'That's not a stamp, Juma. It's a key to other people's land.'

c010-p_juma/7a33719f.speaker: c010-p_juma
c010-p_juma/7a33719f.text: Mama Achola next door? They fight about rent every month. But she brings him tea when he's working late.

c010-p_juma/818d769e.speaker: c010-p_juma
c010-p_juma/818d769e.text: Call my mother. I was there with the cards, having tea.

c010-p_juma/145ee28d.speaker: c010-p_juma
c010-p_juma/145ee28d.text: I was in Ngara with the cards. I came back at twenty to eight and found him.

c010-p_abdullahi/6b31d067.speaker: c010-p_abdullahi
c010-p_abdullahi/6b31d067.text: I walk this row every night. I know every door on it.

c010-p_abdullahi/821d5234.speaker: c010-p_abdullahi
c010-p_abdullahi/821d5234.text: The wedding man shouted at five and went off with his box. He didn't come back.

c010-p_abdullahi/b3536974.speaker: c010-p_abdullahi
c010-p_abdullahi/b3536974.text: Yellow jacket. Haraka. Twenty past seven, out of Rashid's door with a brown envelope, walking fast. I thought, a late delivery.

c010-p_elizabeth/29cd30f6.speaker: c010-p_elizabeth
c010-p_elizabeth/29cd30f6.text: We fought about rent. I'd never hurt him. Here is every sale I made tonight.

c010-p_elizabeth/ba42a32c.speaker: c010-p_elizabeth
c010-p_elizabeth/ba42a32c.text: He was a stubborn old goat and the best stamp fundi on this road. Who will cut my stamps now?

c010-p_elizabeth/faf56d9b.speaker: c010-p_elizabeth
c010-p_elizabeth/faf56d9b.text: We fought about rent like neighbours do. I was serving all evening.

c010-p_hillary/d8a833cf.speaker: c010-p_hillary
c010-p_hillary/d8a833cf.text: Dead? I shouted at him about my cards. My God.

c010-p_hillary/a6dcc93d.speaker: c010-p_hillary
c010-p_hillary/a6dcc93d.text: He promised me a free reprint on Monday. I was rude to him. I'll have to live with that.

c010-p_hillary/3c8c7276.speaker: c010-p_hillary
c010-p_hillary/3c8c7276.text: I shouted, yes. My wedding is in two weeks. Then I went to the coach.

c010-p_tom/16e267e6.speaker: c010-p_tom
c010-p_tom/16e267e6.text: I collect what I'm sent to collect.

pool-m-middle-1/b7a8b9af.text: I can't tell you anything about that.

pool-m-middle-1/3f1fecf9.speaker: pool-m-middle-1
pool-m-middle-1/3f1fecf9.text: I don't know. Ask someone else.

pool-m-middle-1/69b57ef2.text: Nothing. I didn't see anything about that.

mwalimu/f91704bd.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/f91704bd.text: That's the OB. Who, where, when. Tap the folder when you've read it.

mwalimu/d985a7dd.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/d985a7dd.text: This is the stage. Tap anything that looks wrong. Then tap anything that looks normal. Both matter.

mwalimu/31f134bd.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/31f134bd.text: See that line drop into your notebook? Every fact goes there by itself. You don't write, you think.

mwalimu/4c21d246.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/4c21d246.text: People talk. Tap a face to hear what they saw. Ask about anything you've found by dragging it to them.

mwalimu/d0d285c2.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/d0d285c2.text: The charge sheet. Drag a name into the blank. Only names you've actually met are in the bank.

mwalimu/786ad398.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/786ad398.text: Before you send it to the prosecutor, say the reason out loud. If you can't, don't send it.

mwalimu/8468d879.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/8468d879.text: Halima Abdi reads every sheet this unit sends. She doesn't do favours. Good.

mwalimu/7b6bc0ed.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/7b6bc0ed.text: Start with what the killer left in the gutter. Then ask the marshal how drivers mark their things.

mwalimu/80d5a849.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/80d5a849.text: A maroon jacket at twenty past ten, and a tally book that says only two matatus were parked. Put those side by side.

mwalimu/8f51254a.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/8f51254a.text: One blow, two jackets, one spanner. You read the stage like a marshal reads plates. Keep doing that.

halima/e5f2483b.speaker: halima
halima/e5f2483b.text: Kamau's spanner, Kamau's jacket, Kamau's bay. That will hold.

halima/8469e35f.speaker: halima
halima/8469e35f.text: This doesn't hold up. Read me the stage again: who was actually parked there at twenty past ten?

halima/baad276b.speaker: halima
halima/baad276b.text: No. A defence lawyer would walk this one out by lunch. Look at the weapon.

mwalimu/78879d60.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/78879d60.text: Every office block in Nairobi keeps a book at the front desk. Read it like a list of suspects.

mwalimu/09e13e5a.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/09e13e5a.text: A shoe print in the paint, and a pair of shoes in a bin. Whose bin?

mwalimu/eb36a41f.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/eb36a41f.text: Paint dries. Registers don't lie about who came in after seven. Most people forget that.

halima/c695156c.speaker: halima
halima/c695156c.text: One entry after lock-up, one shoe in the paint, the same shoe in her bin. It will hold.

halima/36efb2fc.speaker: halima
halima/36efb2fc.text: This doesn't hold up. Who was actually inside that building after seven?

halima/6b28f957.speaker: halima
halima/6b28f957.text: No. The paint tells you when. The register tells you who. Read them together.

mwalimu/85d2932c.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/85d2932c.text: She was holding something. Every ticket has two halves. Find the other half.

mwalimu/4f568122.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/4f568122.text: Seat fourteen at 05:22, and seat fourteen empty when the bus left. Who books a seat he doesn't take?

mwalimu/75ca6ba2.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/75ca6ba2.text: Seat fourteen. A man who buys a ticket he never uses is telling you something. Listen to paper.

halima/da53ce2a.speaker: halima
halima/da53ce2a.text: The last ticket she ever wrote was his, and he never got on the bus. That will hold.

halima/3798f70d.speaker: halima
halima/3798f70d.text: This doesn't hold up. Who was standing at that counter at 05:22?

halima/3c288805.speaker: halima
halima/3c288805.text: No. Match the paper in her hand to the bus it belongs to.

mwalimu/757876a3.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/757876a3.text: In a blackout everyone needs light. Faith's candle was never lit. So whose candle was it?

mwalimu/7e2c096a.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/7e2c096a.text: Wax from the desk to the 2nd floor, and a stub outside one door. Check the register for that door.

mwalimu/3c91922a.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/3c91922a.text: Wax doesn't climb stairs on its own. Good work in the dark, Detective.

halima/522b0cb7.speaker: halima
halima/522b0cb7.text: The killer brought light, and the light went to his own door. That will hold.

halima/13344fdb.speaker: halima
halima/13344fdb.text: This doesn't hold up. In a blackout, someone needed light. Follow it.

halima/7b9cf2c4.speaker: halima
halima/7b9cf2c4.text: No. Who could actually move around that hotel between ten past and half past eleven?

mwalimu/6d5a3b30.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/6d5a3b30.text: It rained for forty minutes. Look at the ground under him, and ask yourself when he fell.

mwalimu/ce48cb11.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/ce48cb11.text: Alive at 14:35, on the ground before 14:50. Now ask the customer who was standing there.

mwalimu/cea23775.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/cea23775.text: Dry ground under a body in a downpour. You'll remember that one for years. I did.

halima/4f600a6e.speaker: halima
halima/4f600a6e.text: Dry ground, a dry umbrella and a man waiting to be paid. That will hold.

halima/d3a0f413.speaker: halima
halima/d3a0f413.text: This doesn't hold up. When did he fall? The ground is telling you.

halima/24b3d9f3.speaker: halima
halima/24b3d9f3.text: No. Narrow the time first. Then ask who was standing at that kiosk in it.

mwalimu/f123c328.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/f123c328.text: Something is missing from the shelf. Every repair has a number. Flip the tag.

mwalimu/5b25e1a3.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/5b25e1a3.text: Job 318 was a red radio. Who did the neighbour see carrying a red radio?

mwalimu/5f3923b1.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/5f3923b1.text: Small writing on a torn tag. And a calendar on the wall that you probably didn't look at. Everyone looks at the body first.

halima/40a4d5cc.speaker: halima
halima/40a4d5cc.text: A torn tag, the job it belongs to, and the man seen carrying it away. That will hold.

halima/086b82a7.speaker: halima
halima/086b82a7.text: This doesn't hold up. Something was taken off that shelf. What, and whose was it?

halima/3fc5366e.speaker: halima
halima/3fc5366e.text: No. Read the small writing. Then read the job book.

mwalimu/6a9381af.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/6a9381af.text: The killer left something on her. Florists will tell you: that colour doesn't come from roses.

mwalimu/da1c4274.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/da1c4274.text: Her own lilies were still sealed. Read the licence board: who else sells them?

mwalimu/371c5fac.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/371c5fac.text: Scratched hands, and the man was innocent. You'll meet a lot of scratched hands. Be fair to them.

halima/dab2259b.speaker: halima
halima/dab2259b.text: Lily pollen on her shoulder, and one lily seller in the market, seen wiping her hands. That will hold.

halima/e5afaf1c.speaker: halima
halima/e5afaf1c.text: This doesn't hold up. Scratched hands are not a confession. What did the killer leave on her?

halima/425cad6d.speaker: halima
halima/425cad6d.text: No. Where did that pollen come from? Not from her own box.

mwalimu/4bd7560b.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/4bd7560b.text: There's a ticket on that floor. A ticket tells you a train, a time and a window. Ask the window.

mwalimu/c828706c.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/c828706c.text: No punch hole, and inspectors punch every ticket on board. So whoever bought it never got on.

mwalimu/6e0be520.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/6e0be520.text: A ticket with no hole in it. Sometimes the clue is what isn't there. Write that on your wall.

halima/5f41ca0a.speaker: halima
halima/5f41ca0a.text: Her ticket, on the storeroom floor, never punched. She never caught her train. That will hold.

halima/f3863dda.speaker: halima
halima/f3863dda.text: This doesn't hold up. Whose ticket is on that floor?

halima/a0b057d2.speaker: halima
halima/a0b057d2.text: No. Ask the inspector what an unpunched ticket means.

mwalimu/f5bd99d5.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/f5bd99d5.text: Everyone is looking at the brother. Charles wasn't. Read what he wrote on the back page.

mwalimu/e9685aba.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/e9685aba.text: A green overall in the background of a photograph, and only one man in the park who wears green.

mwalimu/138691e1.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/138691e1.text: Everyone wanted it to be the brother. You didn't. That's the job.

halima/2ff2d162.speaker: halima
halima/2ff2d162.text: Not the brother. The man in green, with the tin. That will hold, and I'm glad you didn't send me the brother.

halima/656c9adc.speaker: halima
halima/656c9adc.text: This doesn't hold up. A fight in the morning is not a killing in the afternoon. Where was the brother?

halima/06adf78d.speaker: halima
halima/06adf78d.text: No. Charles wrote down who he suspected. Read the back page, then look at the background of that photo.

mwalimu/6f3e2639.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/6f3e2639.text: Rashid wrote down everyone who collected official stamps. Look under the order book.

mwalimu/ad48cbfc.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/ad48cbfc.text: A courier refused at 19:02, and a courier's jacket leaving at 19:20. Then ask whose order he came for.

mwalimu/34778b02.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/34778b02.text: You've seen that till number before. Write it down somewhere I can't see it.

halima/441c6de6.speaker: halima
halima/441c6de6.text: Ochieng carried it out. But he didn't order it. Who is Mvua Holdings?

halima/2100a313.speaker: halima
halima/2100a313.text: This doesn't hold up. A courier doesn't kill over a parcel unless someone is waiting for it. Look again.

halima/0c1333a2.speaker: halima
halima/0c1333a2.text: No. Both names have to be right. Who came at seven, and for whose order?

c011-p_sharon/9bba35e7.speaker: c011-p_sharon
c011-p_sharon/9bba35e7.text: I heard. Everybody heard. Ask me what you want.

c011-p_sharon/2ad82aa7.speaker: c011-p_sharon
c011-p_sharon/2ad82aa7.text: Two years we were together. Then he wanted a bike, and the bank wanted a name that pays. Mine.

c011-p_sharon/24a52f81.speaker: c011-p_sharon
c011-p_sharon/24a52f81.text: Seventy thousand on a bike I never rode. This morning they carried my fridge out in front of the whole stage. You want me to cry? I'm finished crying.

c011-p_sharon/334d167e.speaker: c011-p_sharon
c011-p_sharon/334d167e.text: Everyone at this stage wears gumboots when it rains. Look at the road.

c011-p_sharon/f41daad9.speaker: c011-p_sharon
c011-p_sharon/f41daad9.text: It's a poker. I poke the jiko with it.

c011-p_sharon/17ad2ff7.speaker: c011-p_sharon
c011-p_sharon/17ad2ff7.text: Erick owed me money. Everyone at this stage knows that.

c011-p_sharon/4c69e665.speaker: c011-p_sharon
c011-p_sharon/4c69e665.text: I closed the kiosk at half past seven and went home to Kayole Junction.

c011-p_sharon/9216f76a.speaker: c011-p_sharon
c011-p_sharon/9216f76a.text: ...Fine. I stayed. He came at quarter past eight with his phone, like nothing happened, like my fridge was still there. We shouted. He laughed and walked off to the trench. I locked up and went home. That is all.

c011-p_jackson/15b125e3.speaker: c011-p_jackson
c011-p_jackson/15b125e3.text: One of mine. Number Seven. What happened?

c011-p_jackson/44e95df1.speaker: c011-p_jackson
c011-p_jackson/44e95df1.text: He owed the stage a thousand. I fined him, yes. That is my job. You do not kill a man over a thousand bob.

c011-p_jackson/def09eee.speaker: c011-p_jackson
c011-p_jackson/def09eee.text: That boy ruined her. She signed for his bike, he stopped paying. The loan people came this morning and took her fridge.

c011-p_jackson/ee628289.speaker: c011-p_jackson
c011-p_jackson/ee628289.text: Twelve and Seven fought on Sunday over a customer. Boys. I warned them both.

c011-p_jackson/1d583e02.speaker: c011-p_jackson
c011-p_jackson/1d583e02.text: I was at the chief's baraza on stage fees all evening.

c011-p_abednego/080ccd53.speaker: c011-p_abednego
c011-p_abednego/080ccd53.text: Number Seven? I don't know anything about Number Seven.

c011-p_abednego/ac094aeb.speaker: c011-p_abednego
c011-p_abednego/ac094aeb.text: Call the girl at the pump. She remembers me. I paid in coins and she was angry.

c011-p_abednego/b1cfff50.speaker: c011-p_abednego
c011-p_abednego/b1cfff50.text: He pushed me first. Over a customer. On Sunday. That doesn't mean I'd put him in a hole.

c011-p_abednego/6fa8fc25.speaker: c011-p_abednego
c011-p_abednego/6fa8fc25.text: I took a customer to Fedha at eight.

c011-p_teresia/b93c8a20.speaker: c011-p_teresia
c011-p_teresia/b93c8a20.text: Nine years on this corner. Nobody ever died in front of me before.

c011-p_teresia/ac9c7475.speaker: c011-p_teresia
c011-p_teresia/ac9c7475.text: He bought maize from me every night. Tonight too, twenty past eight. He walked off eating it, towards the trench, to relieve himself like they all do.

c011-p_teresia/10b8ff88.speaker: c011-p_teresia
c011-p_teresia/10b8ff88.text: Sharon? They were together, before. Her shutter was down when I found him. I didn't see her close it; I was busy with customers.

c012-p_mwita/fc8f695b.speaker: c012-p_mwita
c012-p_mwita/fc8f695b.text: Come in, officer. I know about Margaret. Terrible.

c012-p_mwita/b864bee5.speaker: c012-p_mwita
c012-p_mwita/b864bee5.text: A mistake. The auctioneer doesn't know I paid. I will take the receipt to his office on Monday.

c012-p_mwita/3306a699.speaker: c012-p_mwita
c012-p_mwita/3306a699.text: Eleven years she has been caretaker. She was strict, but she was fair. Until this year.

c012-p_mwita/292d5470.speaker: c012-p_mwita
c012-p_mwita/292d5470.text: Bonface is an old man. He sees a man with a book. Many people carry books.

c012-p_mwita/62fe0602.speaker: c012-p_mwita
c012-p_mwita/62fe0602.text: I paid all my arrears on Saturday. Margaret gave me a receipt.

c012-p_mwita/4a4ae14a.speaker: c012-p_mwita
c012-p_mwita/4a4ae14a.text: Nineteen years I have lived in 4C. I have never been late until this year.

c012-p_mwita/714716f8.speaker: c012-p_mwita
c012-p_mwita/714716f8.text: ...I took the book. Nineteen years in that flat. My arrears were in it. Without the book, who could prove anything? But she was already lying there when I went in. I swear it on my children.

c012-p_lydia/f8bc5061.speaker: c012-p_lydia
c012-p_lydia/f8bc5061.text: I shouted at her on Monday. Everybody heard. Now you think I killed her.

c012-p_lydia/4d03ce24.speaker: c012-p_lydia
c012-p_lydia/4d03ce24.text: Four days without water on my floor. Four days. I shouted, yes. Then I paid her today like always.

c012-p_lydia/de8076c0.speaker: c012-p_lydia
c012-p_lydia/de8076c0.text: There. Twenty past five. Then I went straight to Janeth's in the market.

c012-p_lydia/3af227be.speaker: c012-p_lydia
c012-p_lydia/3af227be.text: Call her. She'll tell you how long braids take.

c012-p_lydia/a78b2502.speaker: c012-p_lydia
c012-p_lydia/a78b2502.text: I paid my rent at twenty past five and went to get my hair done.

c012-p_wilson/eb3482ea.speaker: c012-p_wilson
c012-p_wilson/eb3482ea.text: I fix pipes. I don't know anything.

c012-p_wilson/bf82a584.speaker: c012-p_wilson
c012-p_wilson/bf82a584.text: She owed me for the tank. She said the 10th. I believed her. Now who will pay me?

c012-p_wilson/9a232a0c.speaker: c012-p_wilson
c012-p_wilson/9a232a0c.text: She walked me out herself. She was alive and shouting about my invoice.

c012-p_bonface/3639eafb.speaker: c012-p_bonface
c012-p_bonface/3639eafb.text: I sat here. I watched this gate. Nobody passed.

c012-p_bonface/0e67d917.speaker: c012-p_bonface
c012-p_bonface/0e67d917.text: Mzee Mwita? Nineteen years here. Retired from the railway. A gentleman. At ten past six he went up with that blue book under his jacket. I thought she lent it to him.

c012-p_bonface/ee697226.speaker: c012-p_bonface
c012-p_bonface/ee697226.text: Mama Margaret walked him out herself at 17:41. She was complaining about his invoice the whole way.

c013-p_josephine/fa7f7e4b.speaker: c013-p_josephine
c013-p_josephine/fa7f7e4b.text: Hodan? No. No. Five years I have bought from her.

c013-p_josephine/28e7f3de.speaker: c013-p_josephine
c013-p_josephine/28e7f3de.text: That is a deposit slip. I deposit, the bank stamps, I pay. Ask the bank.

c013-p_josephine/398cf471.speaker: c013-p_josephine
c013-p_josephine/398cf471.text: Maybe they had a late counter. I don't work in a bank.

c013-p_josephine/583b22be.speaker: c013-p_josephine
c013-p_josephine/583b22be.text: Many women wear purple. Go to Gikomba and count them.

c013-p_josephine/501b0413.speaker: c013-p_josephine
c013-p_josephine/501b0413.text: I left Eastleigh at four on the Machakos matatu. By six I was already home.

c013-p_josephine/93dad998.speaker: c013-p_josephine
c013-p_josephine/93dad998.text: I have bought from Hodan for five years. Ask anyone in this mall.

c013-p_josephine/4179de1e.speaker: c013-p_josephine
c013-p_josephine/4179de1e.text: I came back for the bales, yes. Three bales, that is all. She was alive when I left. She was shouting at me, but she was alive.

c013-p_abdirahman/f4aed75a.speaker: c013-p_abdirahman
c013-p_abdirahman/f4aed75a.text: My cousin. We fought over money. That is family. That is not this.

c013-p_abdirahman/05bf1ec7.speaker: c013-p_abdirahman
c013-p_abdirahman/05bf1ec7.text: Our dispute is with the wazee, the elders. Her father's share. We would have settled it in a month.

c013-p_abdirahman/eb94ab8f.speaker: c013-p_abdirahman
c013-p_abdirahman/eb94ab8f.text: Mama Josephine from Machakos? She always paid by slip. Hodan trusted her. Hodan never even went to the bank to check.

c013-p_abdirahman/265993e9.speaker: c013-p_abdirahman
c013-p_abdirahman/265993e9.text: Ask the Sheikh. I came early for Maghrib and sat with him.

c013-p_abdirahman/cb3b7b90.speaker: c013-p_abdirahman
c013-p_abdirahman/cb3b7b90.text: I was at the mosque from before Maghrib.

c013-p_rajesh/699ccad2.speaker: c013-p_rajesh
c013-p_rajesh/699ccad2.text: Everybody got that letter. The shilling falls, I pay more in dollars, the price goes up. Nothing personal.

c013-p_rajesh/de951931.speaker: c013-p_rajesh
c013-p_rajesh/de951931.text: She was the best buyer on First Avenue. She argued, she paid. I am very sorry.

c013-p_rajesh/35b33c6a.speaker: c013-p_rajesh
c013-p_rajesh/35b33c6a.text: I haven't been to Eastleigh in a week. I was at my godown all evening.

c013-p_fatuma/f775f331.speaker: c013-p_fatuma
c013-p_fatuma/f775f331.text: I bring her shaah every evening. Every evening.

c013-p_fatuma/547b3893.speaker: c013-p_fatuma
c013-p_fatuma/547b3893.text: At twenty-five past six she was arguing about the bank with a woman. A woman in purple. I left the glass outside. I didn't want to disturb.

c013-p_lameck/a406b97e.speaker: c013-p_lameck
c013-p_lameck/a406b97e.text: I carried bales for a woman. That is my work. I did nothing.

c013-p_lameck/908ff15b.speaker: c013-p_lameck
c013-p_lameck/908ff15b.text: That is the woman. The purple. She told me Mama Hodan was resting. She paid me three hundred and I took her bales to the Machakos matatus.

c014-p_monicah/057844de.speaker: c014-p_monicah
c014-p_monicah/057844de.text: Sixty people in here, and nobody saw anything. They were all watching the screen.

c014-p_monicah/eaeceb21.speaker: c014-p_monicah
c014-p_monicah/eaeceb21.text: He was hard, but he paid me. His wife wanted to sell this place. Every week, the same fight.

c014-p_monicah/325429e1.speaker: c014-p_monicah
c014-p_monicah/325429e1.text: Mzee fired him at three. No wages for two months. Ian still came and ran the match. I thought, that boy is a saint.

c014-p_monicah/5f03f8da.speaker: c014-p_monicah
c014-p_monicah/5f03f8da.text: Tobias? He shouted at Mzee at half-time about three hundred bob on his tab. After that I didn't see him. I was busy.

c014-p_tobias/c7093136.speaker: c014-p_tobias
c014-p_tobias/c7093136.text: I was here. I was watching the match. Like everybody.

c014-p_tobias/7ea6d96d.speaker: c014-p_tobias
c014-p_tobias/7ea6d96d.text: Three hundred bob. He said I don't pay. I always pay.

c014-p_tobias/c8c76cf4.speaker: c014-p_tobias
c014-p_tobias/c8c76cf4.text: I watched the whole second half from my seat. I never left the pub.

c014-p_tobias/c0c8eb13.speaker: c014-p_tobias
c014-p_tobias/c0c8eb13.text: Mzee and I shouted about a tab. That's football.

c014-p_tobias/51aa6ad8.speaker: c014-p_tobias
c014-p_tobias/51aa6ad8.text: Please. Please don't tell my mother. That was her school-fees money for my sister. I was at Kamari Point the whole time, I swear. Ask the cashier. I lost all of it.

c014-p_ian/264de8d0.speaker: c014-p_ian
c014-p_ian/264de8d0.text: The stream drops when the Wi-Fi drops. Every match. Ask anyone.

c014-p_ian/3443dd99.speaker: c014-p_ian
c014-p_ian/3443dd99.text: Anyone could have put them there. I leave them everywhere.

c014-p_ian/0f5bbab5.speaker: c014-p_ian
c014-p_ian/0f5bbab5.text: He fired me at three. I still ran his match. Does that sound like a man who is angry?

c014-p_ian/df42e016.speaker: c014-p_ian
c014-p_ian/df42e016.text: I had no problem with Mzee.

c014-p_purity/a3b43879.speaker: c014-p_purity
c014-p_purity/a3b43879.text: They called me during the last hymn.

c014-p_purity/6a05e6dd.speaker: c014-p_purity
c014-p_purity/6a05e6dd.text: Twenty-three years married. Yes, I wanted to sell. A buyer offered good money. He said he would die in that pub first.

c014-p_purity/896743e2.speaker: c014-p_purity
c014-p_purity/896743e2.text: Call the deacon. He keeps the door. He counts us in and out like sheep.

c014-p_purity/d4f485fd.speaker: c014-p_purity
c014-p_purity/d4f485fd.text: I was at church until half past nine.

c014-p_cynthia/67a0ca8b.speaker: c014-p_cynthia
c014-p_cynthia/67a0ca8b.text: I see a hundred faces a night. Ask me about one.

c014-p_cynthia/52f8147f.speaker: c014-p_cynthia
c014-p_cynthia/52f8147f.text: The mechanic. He stood right here from quarter to nine until after nine, staring at the odds. Second-half bets. The last one was big.

c015-p_felistus/82408a0f.speaker: c015-p_felistus
c015-p_felistus/82408a0f.text: Hezron? Dead? God forgive me, I said things about him yesterday.

c015-p_felistus/655590be.speaker: c015-p_felistus
c015-p_felistus/655590be.text: Many bales have seals. Many numbers.

c015-p_felistus/d21821f0.speaker: c015-p_felistus
c015-p_felistus/d21821f0.text: Thirty-eight thousand. A chama loan. "First grade." I opened it and it was rags. He said sell rags as rags.

c015-p_felistus/bc3b7dcc.speaker: c015-p_felistus
c015-p_felistus/bc3b7dcc.text: Hamisi pushes everyone's bales. He sees everyone. What does he say?

c015-p_felistus/c839430f.speaker: c015-p_felistus
c015-p_felistus/c839430f.text: He cheated me. I won't pretend he didn't.

c015-p_felistus/40381a11.speaker: c015-p_felistus
c015-p_felistus/40381a11.text: This morning I opened at my own stall at five. I never went down to his godown.

c015-p_felistus/bd135388.speaker: c015-p_felistus
c015-p_felistus/bd135388.text: I went to show him the seal. That is all. I begged him. Thirty-eight thousand, my chama's money. He laughed at me. Then I left. Before five, I swear.

c015-p_lucas/3c0b1c80.speaker: c015-p_lucas
c015-p_lucas/3c0b1c80.text: I got off the bus and came straight here. Straight here.

c015-p_lucas/160d2626.speaker: c015-p_lucas
c015-p_lucas/160d2626.text: He never took it off. He slept with it. Whoever did this knew it was there.

c015-p_lucas/c0bdaf35.speaker: c015-p_lucas
c015-p_lucas/c0bdaf35.text: We argued about the split. Sixty-forty, seventy-thirty. Business. I was in Mombasa buying his bales.

c015-p_lucas/56e81b6f.speaker: c015-p_lucas
c015-p_lucas/56e81b6f.text: I was on the overnight bus from Mombasa. I came straight here.

c015-p_winnie/1840c329.speaker: c015-p_winnie
c015-p_winnie/1840c329.text: I don't talk about that man.

c015-p_winnie/ffc4b875.speaker: c015-p_winnie
c015-p_winnie/ffc4b875.text: Felistus lost everything on that bale. The whole market knew. She cried at my stall for an hour.

c015-p_winnie/6dfd3936.speaker: c015-p_winnie
c015-p_winnie/6dfd3936.text: Ask Mama Esther next door. She watched me sell all morning.

c015-p_winnie/00bd58a1.speaker: c015-p_winnie
c015-p_winnie/00bd58a1.text: I don't go near his godown since he cut me off. I opened my stall at quarter to five.

c015-p_hamisi/86ef491e.speaker: c015-p_hamisi
c015-p_hamisi/86ef491e.text: I push bales. Every morning, the same. This morning was not the same.

c015-p_hamisi/dafb4898.speaker: c015-p_hamisi
c015-p_hamisi/dafb4898.text: That is the woman. She was shouting about rags. Then she passed me in the lane, fast, holding a pouch against her chest. I thought, she got her money back.

c015-p_hamisi/8311a383.speaker: c015-p_hamisi
c015-p_hamisi/8311a383.text: Two bales for Mzee Daudi, upper market. Call him. I delivered at five.

c016-p_baraka/3f535d77.speaker: c016-p_baraka
c016-p_baraka/3f535d77.text: I already told them. Write it down.

c016-p_baraka/595726db.speaker: c016-p_baraka
c016-p_baraka/595726db.text: Leave her. She is old. She didn't do anything.

c016-p_baraka/3faf517f.speaker: c016-p_baraka
c016-p_baraka/3faf517f.text: I did it. I hit him with the valve key. Leave my grandmother out of this.

c016-p_baraka/218b310b.speaker: c016-p_baraka
c016-p_baraka/218b310b.text: ...I wasn't there when it happened. Bibi called me after. She told me to go home and say nothing. I couldn't let them take her. She is all I have.

c016-p_kadzo/6b3ec699.speaker: c016-p_kadzo
c016-p_kadzo/6b3ec699.text: Nobody else touches it. The committee says so. Fourteen years, it hangs on my wall.

c016-p_kadzo/844642ec.speaker: c016-p_kadzo
c016-p_kadzo/844642ec.text: She goes quiet for a long time. "He is a good boy. He brings me tea.

c016-p_kadzo/c2e14849.speaker: c016-p_kadzo
c016-p_kadzo/c2e14849.text: Monday. Because he would not give that man our takings. Two thousand shillings. For water.

c016-p_kadzo/f154d8b8.speaker: c016-p_kadzo
c016-p_kadzo/f154d8b8.text: That man broke my grandson's arm on Monday. Because the boy would not give him our takings.

c016-p_kadzo/119b936a.speaker: c016-p_kadzo
c016-p_kadzo/119b936a.text: I sell water. That is all I do.

c016-p_nicholas/46ef0039.speaker: c016-p_nicholas
c016-p_nicholas/46ef0039.text: Mulwa? Huh. Everyone on that river had a reason.

c016-p_nicholas/3a822649.speaker: c016-p_nicholas
c016-p_nicholas/3a822649.text: Everyone on this river had a reason. Not everyone had the stomach.

c016-p_nicholas/3d9ae647.speaker: c016-p_nicholas
c016-p_nicholas/3d9ae647.text: Call Mama Akinyi. It is her brother's matanga. I have been leading the songs all night.

c016-p_nicholas/701f4249.speaker: c016-p_nicholas
c016-p_nicholas/701f4249.text: I was at a matanga in Huruma all night.

c016-p_zipporah/10df9a40.speaker: c016-p_zipporah
c016-p_zipporah/10df9a40.text: I heard it. I hear everything at that kiosk. These walls are tin.

c016-p_zipporah/a17b422e.speaker: c016-p_zipporah
c016-p_zipporah/a17b422e.text: The nurse at the clinic set the boy's arm on Monday. Ask her what he said.

c017-p_evans/f2d9e769.speaker: c017-p_evans
c017-p_evans/f2d9e769.text: I am a businessman. I have nothing to say.

c017-p_evans/b783e3a3.speaker: c017-p_evans
c017-p_evans/b783e3a3.text: Searches go wrong. Clerks make mistakes. Land is complicated.

c017-p_evans/0073b3d8.speaker: c017-p_evans
c017-p_evans/0073b3d8.text: Every paper is stamped. Certified. Look at it.

c017-p_evans/6a77329c.speaker: c017-p_evans
c017-p_evans/6a77329c.text: Badges. Everyone has badges in this place.

c017-p_evans/cb2557f8.speaker: c017-p_evans
c017-p_evans/cb2557f8.text: That plot is clean. She was confused.

c017-p_philip/d2c39e7a.speaker: c017-p_philip
c017-p_philip/d2c39e7a.text: Evans? Yes, he was here. All evening.

c017-p_philip/7337c9fd.speaker: c017-p_philip
c017-p_philip/7337c9fd.text: We were at school together in Kakamega. He sells plots. He does well.

c017-p_philip/ec39cec3.speaker: c017-p_philip
c017-p_philip/ec39cec3.text: Evans was with me in my flat, A-3-02, from seven until ten. We watched the news and the football.

c017-p_philip/ff78ad30.speaker: c017-p_philip
c017-p_philip/ff78ad30.text: ...I fell asleep after the seven o'clock news. When I woke up he was there, sweating, on my sofa. He asked me to say he had been there the whole time. I didn't ask why. I didn't want to know why.

c017-p_martin/e99ab726.speaker: c017-p_martin
c017-p_martin/e99ab726.text: We argued about the fees. Shouted, even. But I would never touch her. She is my son's mother.

c017-p_martin/d3fbe2a0.speaker: c017-p_martin
c017-p_martin/d3fbe2a0.text: I was at work all night.

c017-p_saida/d5023487.speaker: c017-p_saida
c017-p_saida/d5023487.text: I heard it all through that wall. I just didn't know what I was hearing.

c017-p_saida/cda57703.speaker: c017-p_saida
c017-p_saida/cda57703.text: A man in a grey suit came to see her last month with papers. She was so happy that day. "My plot," she said.

c017-p_julius/adf93b9f.speaker: c017-p_julius
c017-p_julius/adf93b9f.text: Fourteen. Every badge comes back. Every one. Except tonight.

c017-p_julius/a854bda2.speaker: c017-p_julius
c017-p_julius/a854bda2.text: He signed in at ten past eight for C-11-04. Polite. A suit. I gave him fourteen.

c017-p_julius/f22887c6.speaker: c017-p_julius
c017-p_julius/f22887c6.text: Mzee Philip in Tower A? To get to Tower C you cross my yard. Nobody from A crossed it before that van came. After that, I was busy shouting at a driver.

c018-p_mercy/4ea71a5e.speaker: c018-p_mercy
c018-p_mercy/4ea71a5e.text: Shaddy? Who did this to him?

c018-p_mercy/0d5dec75.speaker: c018-p_mercy
c018-p_mercy/0d5dec75.text: That is my song. My words, my melody. He put another man's name on it and called me backing vocals.

c018-p_mercy/c150d05f.speaker: c018-p_mercy
c018-p_mercy/c150d05f.text: Gold hoops? Every manzi in Nairobi has gold hoops.

c018-p_mercy/7e8dc156.speaker: c018-p_mercy
c018-p_mercy/7e8dc156.text: Silver is in this year. Go to any show.

c018-p_mercy/8624efec.speaker: c018-p_mercy
c018-p_mercy/8624efec.text: I was at the Kasarani show until midnight. Ask my manager, Rosemary.

c018-p_mercy/4a7045f0.speaker: c018-p_mercy
c018-p_mercy/4a7045f0.text: Shaddy stole my song. I wanted my name on it, not his blood.

c018-p_mercy/180d5fc6.speaker: c018-p_mercy
c018-p_mercy/180d5fc6.text: I went to the studio after my set. Fine. I signed in for a retake so he would have to see me. We fought about the song. I left before half eleven. He was alive. He was laughing at me.

c018-p_clinton/867874d2.speaker: c018-p_clinton
c018-p_clinton/867874d2.text: I came to record. That's all. I came to record.

c018-p_clinton/eed8f397.speaker: c018-p_clinton
c018-p_clinton/eed8f397.text: He took everyone's money. Not everyone's songs. Mine he just never recorded.

c018-p_clinton/2b4a4335.speaker: c018-p_clinton
c018-p_clinton/2b4a4335.text: Erastus brought me. Call him. We left Kariobangi ten to twelve.

c018-p_clinton/10998df0.speaker: c018-p_clinton
c018-p_clinton/10998df0.text: I came for my midnight session and found him. Ask my rider.

c018-p_rosemary/fc01a0d0.speaker: c018-p_rosemary
c018-p_rosemary/fc01a0d0.text: Mercy? She left straight after her set. She was crying. I thought it was nerves.

c018-p_rosemary/6b11e2a5.speaker: c018-p_rosemary
c018-p_rosemary/6b11e2a5.text: He owed me forty thousand from April. You don't kill a man you're waiting to get paid by.

c018-p_rosemary/fdb49523.speaker: c018-p_rosemary
c018-p_rosemary/fdb49523.text: I was paying performers at Kasarani until after midnight.

c018-p_sophie/b03b3e6a.speaker: c018-p_sophie
c018-p_sophie/b03b3e6a.text: Two years of bass through my floor. Tonight it was shouting instead.

c018-p_sophie/6c8a671f.speaker: c018-p_sophie
c018-p_sophie/6c8a671f.text: His girlfriend. The singer. She is here more than he is.

c019-p_benson/38e99da0.speaker: c019-p_benson
c019-p_benson/38e99da0.text: Wanjiku? God rest her. We competed. That is business.

c019-p_benson/5addd812.speaker: c019-p_benson
c019-p_benson/5addd812.text: Bad work. Soft metal, too thin. I have been saying it to the county for a month.

c019-p_benson/5daa034f.speaker: c019-p_benson
c019-p_benson/5daa034f.text: Call the clerk at City Hall, Koech. He will tell you I was there.

c019-p_benson/add36a1f.speaker: c019-p_benson
c019-p_benson/add36a1f.text: Dismissed. They didn't even read it.

c019-p_benson/4d7479bf.speaker: c019-p_benson
c019-p_benson/4d7479bf.text: I was at City Hall all afternoon about my appeal. I didn't come back to Kamukunji until four.

c019-p_benson/977bf833.speaker: c019-p_benson
c019-p_benson/977bf833.text: She won with bribes. Everyone knows.

c019-p_benson/b6714391.speaker: c019-p_benson
c019-p_benson/b6714391.text: I left early, yes. Twenty to two. They threw out my appeal in ten minutes. I came back and went to tell her what I thought of her stoves. Yes, I went in. She was alive when I walked out.

c019-p_gitau/030a2c8b.speaker: c019-p_gitau
c019-p_gitau/030a2c8b.text: I was at the clinic with our girl. They called me there.

c019-p_gitau/36341355.speaker: c019-p_gitau
c019-p_gitau/36341355.text: I took it. Two hundred thousand. A debt from before, men were coming to the house. I was going to put it back before she noticed.

c019-p_gitau/93e4a9d5.speaker: c019-p_gitau
c019-p_gitau/93e4a9d5.text: I was at the clinic with our daughter all afternoon.

c019-p_fidel/1fccb2f3.speaker: c019-p_fidel
c019-p_fidel/1fccb2f3.text: I took the stoves. I came back. That is all I know.

c019-p_fidel/291af04e.speaker: c019-p_fidel
c019-p_fidel/291af04e.text: Mama never left dents like that. Never. She would have beaten them out before lunch.

c019-p_fidel/343aa0e9.speaker: c019-p_fidel
c019-p_fidel/343aa0e9.text: She docked me for a spoiled batch. I was angry one day. Then she bought me lunch.

c019-p_fidel/f279cc37.speaker: c019-p_fidel
c019-p_fidel/f279cc37.text: I was delivering stoves to the school.

c019-p_simeon/7edb1fcc.speaker: c019-p_simeon
c019-p_simeon/7edb1fcc.text: This is not her hammer. I know her hammer.

c019-p_simeon/4ec81ff8.speaker: c019-p_simeon
c019-p_simeon/4ec81ff8.text: Every hammer wears its own face. An X like that is a chip. Okiror's has an X. He chipped it on a rivet last year and was too proud to grind it.

c019-p_simeon/7ce140a7.speaker: c019-p_simeon
c019-p_simeon/7ce140a7.text: The school driver took a sample at two. Call him; the number is on her job card.

c020-p_millicent/44add659.speaker: c020-p_millicent
c020-p_millicent/44add659.text: Anne? Our Anne? I was going to see her on Thursday at the payout.

c020-p_millicent/09c99e13.speaker: c020-p_millicent
c020-p_millicent/09c99e13.text: For safekeeping. During the investment. It was voted. It is in the minutes.

c020-p_millicent/bd44211a.speaker: c020-p_millicent
c020-p_millicent/bd44211a.text: I never met anyone from Mvua. The letters came signed "K". The plot fees were collected in cash by a man they call Fundi. He has a bad leg. That is all I know.

c020-p_millicent/f576cb2a.speaker: c020-p_millicent
c020-p_millicent/f576cb2a.text: Anne voted for the Mvua investment at the April meeting. She agreed to everything.

c020-p_millicent/7546796a.speaker: c020-p_millicent
c020-p_millicent/7546796a.text: I was at home all evening.

c020-p_millicent/7fc3eb3c.speaker: c020-p_millicent
c020-p_millicent/7fc3eb3c.text: ...She wasn't there. We needed the vote before the offer closed. It is a good investment. The plots are real. I have seen the papers.

c020-p_millicent/5a98b71b.speaker: c020-p_millicent
c020-p_millicent/5a98b71b.text: I went for the ledger. Quarter past eight. She was going to read it to everybody on Thursday and nobody would understand it. We argued. I took it. That is all I will say.

c020-p_joyce/4f216313.speaker: c020-p_joyce
c020-p_joyce/4f216313.text: I am the secretary. I write things down.

c020-p_joyce/1283cc58.speaker: c020-p_joyce
c020-p_joyce/1283cc58.text: I gave her my key in April. There is no copy. You can't copy those keys on River Road. They're the old kind.

c020-p_joyce/24b73a90.speaker: c020-p_joyce
c020-p_joyce/24b73a90.text: Anne came back from Eldoret and asked to see every receipt. She stopped talking to Millicent after that.

c020-p_joyce/801a520f.speaker: c020-p_joyce
c020-p_joyce/801a520f.text: I don't have my key. The chair does.

c020-p_musau/0ff37df3.speaker: c020-p_musau
c020-p_musau/0ff37df3.text: Anne. Anne. I was at the microphone. I was at the microphone.

c020-p_musau/22795c24.speaker: c020-p_musau
c020-p_musau/22795c24.text: I took a loan against her share. I lost it. Betting. She shouted, I shouted. That was the last thing I said to her.

c020-p_musau/cf72eafe.speaker: c020-p_musau
c020-p_musau/cf72eafe.text: I was the MC at my cousin's funeral harambee in Kangundo.

c020-p_florence/29b75fe2.speaker: c020-p_florence
c020-p_florence/29b75fe2.text: Anne is dead? Then where is our money?

c020-p_florence/d5e70661.speaker: c020-p_florence
c020-p_florence/d5e70661.text: Because Millicent kept saying the money was "invested". I wanted mine before it disappeared. Anne was the only one who believed me.

c020-p_gladys/5b215e29.speaker: c020-p_gladys
c020-p_gladys/5b215e29.text: Twenty-four women own that kitenge. I own one. I couldn't see her face.

c020-p_gladys/03bba96b.speaker: c020-p_gladys
c020-p_gladys/03bba96b.text: He was not here tonight. He left at four for the funeral in Kangundo. They shouted before he left.

c020-p_jillo/9612e463.speaker: c020-p_jillo
c020-p_jillo/9612e463.text: Eight o'clock, everyone comes for milk. Mama Anne too.

c020-p_jillo/529cf846.speaker: c020-p_jillo
c020-p_jillo/529cf846.text: Five past eight. One packet of milk. She said, "I'm going home to count." She was smiling.

pool-f-young-3/faf8c3b1.speaker: pool-f-young-3
pool-f-young-3/faf8c3b1.text: I can't tell you anything about that.

pool-f-young-3/ac5d63f3.speaker: pool-f-young-3
pool-f-young-3/ac5d63f3.text: I don't know. Ask someone else.

pool-f-young-3/d6e48ea0.speaker: pool-f-young-3
pool-f-young-3/d6e48ea0.text: Nothing. I didn't see anything about that.

pool-m-elder-4/341c6b49.speaker: pool-m-elder-4
pool-m-elder-4/341c6b49.text: I can't tell you anything about that.

pool-m-elder-4/aa9c820b.speaker: pool-m-elder-4
pool-m-elder-4/aa9c820b.text: I don't know. Ask someone else.

pool-m-elder-4/ebefbff8.speaker: pool-m-elder-4
pool-m-elder-4/ebefbff8.text: Nothing. I didn't see anything about that.

pool-f-young-4/9e2b6150.speaker: pool-f-young-4
pool-f-young-4/9e2b6150.text: I can't tell you anything about that.

pool-f-young-4/92df31b6.speaker: pool-f-young-4
pool-f-young-4/92df31b6.text: I don't know. Ask someone else.

pool-f-young-4/013d96af.speaker: pool-f-young-4
pool-f-young-4/013d96af.text: Nothing. I didn't see anything about that.

pool-asian-m-any-2/9d698518.speaker: pool-asian-m-any-2
pool-asian-m-any-2/9d698518.text: I can't tell you anything about that.

pool-asian-m-any-2/ef23edbe.speaker: pool-asian-m-any-2
pool-asian-m-any-2/ef23edbe.text: I don't know. Ask someone else.

pool-asian-m-any-2/f16786b7.speaker: pool-asian-m-any-2
pool-asian-m-any-2/f16786b7.text: Nothing. I didn't see anything about that.

pool-f-elder-2/2f060bd6.speaker: pool-f-elder-2
pool-f-elder-2/2f060bd6.text: I can't tell you anything about that.

pool-f-elder-2/1d3b04f4.speaker: pool-f-elder-2
pool-f-elder-2/1d3b04f4.text: I don't know. Ask someone else.

pool-f-elder-2/bc786559.speaker: pool-f-elder-2
pool-f-elder-2/bc786559.text: Nothing. I didn't see anything about that.

pool-f-elder-3/997f8bad.speaker: pool-f-elder-3
pool-f-elder-3/997f8bad.text: I can't tell you anything about that.

pool-f-elder-3/8f66f83f.speaker: pool-f-elder-3
pool-f-elder-3/8f66f83f.text: I don't know. Ask someone else.

pool-f-elder-3/a0d640d4.speaker: pool-f-elder-3
pool-f-elder-3/a0d640d4.text: Nothing. I didn't see anything about that.

mwalimu/f589cd8b.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/f589cd8b.text: From today, people will lie to you. Each person has a statement sheet. Drag a fact onto a claim to press it.

mwalimu/5ca70840.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/5ca70840.text: Read the claims. Then find the one fact that cannot be true at the same time. Only then press.

mwalimu/71ef1279.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/71ef1279.text: That cost you a stamp. Press only when the fact and the claim cannot both be true.

mwalimu/f8403001.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/f8403001.text: Good. A broken claim is a lie, not a confession. Ask yourself what the lie was hiding.

mwalimu/a92efe08.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/a92efe08.text: She says she went home at half seven. She runs a charging kiosk. Charging kiosks keep books.

mwalimu/24556bca.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/24556bca.text: Read the county sign again: where does grey clay come from? Then look at whose boots are carrying it.

mwalimu/e9fa161c.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/e9fa161c.text: She lied about the time and told the truth about the money. Which one did you need?

halima/ae34f239.speaker: halima
halima/ae34f239.text: The book puts her at the kiosk, the boots put her in the trench. That will hold.

halima/9533e30e.speaker: halima
halima/9533e30e.text: Doesn't hold up. Somebody went down into that trench and came back out. Who carried the clay home?

halima/fa083cd9.speaker: halima
halima/fa083cd9.text: No. A man with a grudge isn't a man at the scene. Check where everyone actually was at half past eight.

mwalimu/4653d760.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/4653d760.text: That is grounds: someone saw him with it. A warrant costs a stamp. Spend it when what you find can change the case.

mwalimu/6ec7edfd.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/6ec7edfd.text: Signed. Search it like a scene. Look where a careful man would hide something flat.

mwalimu/7c3f80c2.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/7c3f80c2.text: The watchman sat at the only gate. Ask him who came in, who went out, and who was already inside.

mwalimu/5e8e24fa.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/5e8e24fa.text: A receipt has a number. The book has carbons. On Saturday, how far had the numbers got?

mwalimu/12e71bfa.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/12e71bfa.text: You spent a stamp on that warrant. It was worth it. Remember that it cost something.

halima/b645d0cd.speaker: halima
halima/b645d0cd.text: Nobody came in, nobody went out, and one man was inside with the book. "Already lying there" won't survive that gate book.

halima/4dfd4bc5.speaker: halima
halima/4dfd4bc5.text: Doesn't hold up. Read the gate book against the watchman. Who was inside that compound between 17:41 and 18:10?

halima/d9e5c0d3.speaker: halima
halima/d9e5c0d3.text: No. Shouting about water isn't being in the office. Where was everyone when she died?

mwalimu/487dc7ae.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/487dc7ae.text: Hodan wrote on the slip before she died. Then walk down to the ground floor and read the glass.

mwalimu/f26da9cc.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/f26da9cc.text: The tea seller heard a woman at 18:25. The porter saw a woman at 18:40. Describe them both. Then look at who came to the gate.

mwalimu/045b35ce.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/045b35ce.text: Document services. Interesting thing to sell next to loans.

halima/35d91ad3.speaker: halima
halima/35d91ad3.text: A slip from a shut bank, a woman in purple at 18:25 and again at 18:40, and a lie about the matatu. That will hold.

halima/f4f7e244.speaker: halima
halima/f4f7e244.text: Doesn't hold up. A family dispute with the elders isn't a woman in purple in the cubicle. Read the tea seller and the porter together.

halima/3aab0fa1.speaker: halima
halima/3aab0fa1.text: No. Who was arguing with her about the bank, and who came out of that cubicle alone?

mwalimu/c805f68f.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/c805f68f.text: Some people will not talk until you put something in front of them. Show him what you already know.

mwalimu/6177d45a.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/6177d45a.text: A man who lies to you isn't always a man who kills. Find out what he was hiding before you decide what it means.

mwalimu/94b35119.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/94b35119.text: Somebody in that pub was counting minutes. Turn the match minutes into clock times.

mwalimu/ae063658.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/ae063658.text: The booth was empty while the screen was frozen. Then look behind the crates for something that belongs in the booth.

mwalimu/c6ddbbe8.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/c6ddbbe8.text: You let the liar go. Most people can't. Why could you?

halima/301e3d79.speaker: halima
halima/301e3d79.text: Six minutes of frozen screen, an empty booth beside the storeroom, and his headphones behind the crates. That will hold.

halima/aabced75.speaker: halima
halima/aabced75.text: Doesn't hold up. Your liar was across the road losing his mother's money. A lie isn't a killing.

halima/a918cb66.speaker: halima
halima/a918cb66.text: No. Sixty people were looking at one screen. Who was the only person whose job was not to look at it?

mwalimu/20614071.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/20614071.text: Every seal has a number, and Hezron wrote every number down. Match the one on the floor.

mwalimu/044ff349.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/044ff349.text: He wrote her name at 04:40. The porter saw her with a pouch at 04:55. Now you have grounds.

mwalimu/b917da9d.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/b917da9d.text: Numbers don't lie, Detective. The people who write them down sometimes do. Which was this?

halima/89c8abe8.speaker: halima
halima/89c8abe8.text: His note puts her there, the porter puts the pouch in her hands, and the warrant puts it in her box. That will hold.

halima/08705a9b.speaker: halima
halima/08705a9b.text: Doesn't hold up. A partner on a bus isn't a partner in the godown. Who was there at ten to five?

halima/22b1bf3a.speaker: halima
halima/22b1bf3a.text: No. Follow the seal number, then follow the pouch.

mwalimu/f3ddb6eb.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/f3ddb6eb.text: Pick the key up. Turn it over. Then look at the boy who says he swung it.

mwalimu/26214525.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/26214525.text: Read the notice on the tank. Then ask the neighbour who was at the counter between ten past and quarter past nine.

mwalimu/4f0150ea.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/4f0150ea.text: The boy lied for love. The law doesn't have a box for that. You'll meet it again.

halima/51fa4724.speaker: halima
halima/51fa4724.text: The court will hear what he did to that boy. It still has to hear what she did.

halima/79d87fa4.speaker: halima
halima/79d87fa4.text: A confession is where you start, not where you stop. Look at his arm.

halima/bcefb5db.speaker: halima
halima/bcefb5db.text: No. Who holds that key, and who was at that counter when the clang came?

mwalimu/a24af8a2.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/a24af8a2.text: Philip says his friend was in Tower A all evening. The gate keeps its own book. Read it.

mwalimu/7c5be622.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/7c5be622.text: Badge 14 went out at the gate at 20:10 and never came back. Where did it end up?

mwalimu/79687e70.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/79687e70.text: One friend fell asleep and another one lied. Write down which kind you'd trust next time.

halima/7bbb05ab.speaker: halima
halima/7bbb05ab.text: A friend's alibi that fell asleep, a gate book that didn't, and badge fourteen under her sofa. That will hold.

halima/0f1663e2.speaker: halima
halima/0f1663e2.text: Doesn't hold up. A man who lies for a friend has a friend. Who did he lie for?

halima/a10e025b.speaker: halima
halima/a10e025b.text: No. The ex-husband was clocked in at the airport. Follow the badge.

mwalimu/487a0158.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/487a0158.text: Artists sign the clipboard themselves. Read who came at eleven, and how she signs her name.

mwalimu/c7b60c1b.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/c7b60c1b.text: One earring under the desk. Now look closely at everyone who walks through that door.

mwalimu/0cc7e258.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/0cc7e258.text: Your first case where a face was the evidence. Never stop looking at faces.

halima/0fbd9038.speaker: halima
halima/0fbd9038.text: Her name on the clipboard, her jacket at the corner, and her other earring under his desk. That will hold.

halima/626ca071.speaker: halima
halima/626ca071.text: Doesn't hold up. The man who found him arrived after the crash. Who was there when it happened?

halima/bdad72b2.speaker: halima
halima/bdad72b2.text: No. Look at the earring. Then look at everyone's ears.

mwalimu/eedef9ca.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/eedef9ca.text: Look at the middle of every dent. Then ask the oldest man in the sheds what he sees.

mwalimu/89f9e2b5.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/89f9e2b5.text: An X in every dent, and an old fundi who knows whose hammer has an X. You have grounds for the toolbox.

mwalimu/9fb99a37.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/9fb99a37.text: Every fundi signs his work. So does every detective. What did you sign today?

halima/56d81913.speaker: halima
halima/56d81913.text: He lied about City Hall, he walked in with a hammer, and his hammer signed every dent. That will hold.

halima/4a4edcab.speaker: halima
halima/4a4edcab.text: Doesn't hold up. A husband who stole from her is a thief. Was he in that shed?

halima/7568d629.speaker: halima
halima/7568d629.text: No. Read the dents. Every hammer in that market signs its work.

mwalimu/a5d5a2cf.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/a5d5a2cf.text: Turn the box. Look at each padlock. Two were opened one way, one another.

mwalimu/c3a62075.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/c3a62075.text: Two keys, used. Now read the April minutes: who has been holding two keys since then?

mwalimu/c7ca332b.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/c7ca332b.text: Read the receipts from her house. Then go to the Pattern File.

mwalimu/246b1c71.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/246b1c71.text: Several pins show the till. Only one shows money going into it.

mwalimu/f2c6c337.speaker: mwalimu
mwalimu/f2c6c337.text: Two keys and a cut lock. And a till number you keep seeing. Sleep, Detective. Then read the Pattern File again.

halima/3569f4f8.speaker: halima
halima/3569f4f8.text: Two keys turned, one lock cut, and the minutes say who held two keys. The ledger was in her kitchen. That will hold.

halima/3decde08.speaker: halima
halima/3decde08.text: Doesn't hold up. Look at the box again: two locks opened with keys. Who had two keys?

halima/027f8c42.speaker: halima
halima/027f8c42.text: No. A husband who lost money isn't a woman in the chama kitenge at 20:40. Who could open that box?

halima/a83207f0.speaker: halima
halima/a83207f0.text: The same till that ordered a fake seal is selling fake plots. Amani, who are these people?

halima/11c39d45.speaker: halima
halima/11c39d45.text: She did it. But you're telling me this is bigger than a chama. Show me how.

halima/73562d91.speaker: halima
halima/73562d91.text: That pin shows the till number. I asked which one shows money going into it.

c021-p_dancan/bac08905.speaker: c021-p_dancan
c021-p_dancan/bac08905.text: Six years I worked for her. She trusted me with everything.

c021-p_dancan/2b829e16.speaker: c021-p_dancan
c021-p_dancan/2b829e16.text: Statements? Mama did the books. I sold cloth.

c021-p_dancan/0b16b3a1.speaker: c021-p_dancan
c021-p_dancan/0b16b3a1.text: Her nephew wants the shop. On Tuesday he shouted at her in the street. Everybody heard.

c021-p_dancan/63e317b0.speaker: c021-p_dancan
c021-p_dancan/63e317b0.text: Ask Kassim, the supplier at the bus park. He saw me there. I was waiting an hour.

c021-p_dancan/c89af6af.speaker: c021-p_dancan
c021-p_dancan/c89af6af.text: I was at Mwembe Tayari from half past twelve, waiting for the Malindi bus with our stock.

c021-p_dancan/35073466.speaker: c021-p_dancan
c021-p_dancan/35073466.text: The till works fine. Mama handled all the money.

c021-p_dancan/9e02b70d.speaker: c021-p_dancan
c021-p_dancan/9e02b70d.text: I passed the shop at one. For a minute. To collect the bale list. She was fine when I left. She gave me tea.

c021-p_dancan/ffe5c1c2.speaker: c021-p_dancan
c021-p_dancan/ffe5c1c2.text: Sometimes the till was slow. Customers were waiting. I was helping them. I was going to give her the money.

c021-p_faiz/f52e91f7.speaker: c021-p_faiz
c021-p_faiz/f52e91f7.text: I shouted at her on Tuesday. The last thing I did was shout.

c021-p_faiz/cb831e66.speaker: c021-p_faiz
c021-p_faiz/cb831e66.text: Half the shop, one day. I wanted to run it now, not when she's dead. I'm ashamed of what I said.

c021-p_faiz/272f3b2f.speaker: c021-p_faiz
c021-p_faiz/272f3b2f.text: Ask Ustadh Salim. I recited before the sermon. Three hundred people watched me.

c021-p_rukia/edd9648c.speaker: c021-p_rukia
c021-p_rukia/edd9648c.text: I am with my sister. What is it?

c021-p_rukia/bc35a090.speaker: c021-p_rukia
c021-p_rukia/bc35a090.text: Mama Mwanajuma told me to pay when I can. She was like that. Who does that any more?

c021-p_rukia/515a80fa.speaker: c021-p_rukia
c021-p_rukia/515a80fa.text: I was with my sister. She had a baby girl at two o'clock.

c021-p_abubakar/0371e161.speaker: c021-p_abubakar
c021-p_abubakar/0371e161.text: Forty years next door. Every Friday she stayed in with her books.

c021-p_abubakar/aa7e5f01.speaker: c021-p_abubakar
c021-p_abubakar/aa7e5f01.text: The manager. Polite boy. On Saturdays he runs the shop alone and it is always full.

c021-p_pili/d3fb64fd.speaker: c021-p_pili
c021-p_pili/d3fb64fd.text: Dancan? Yes, I know him. The till never works when I come.

c021-p_pili/b6effea9.speaker: c021-p_pili
c021-p_pili/b6effea9.text: That sign! Twice this month he told me the till was broken and to pay his number. Look, here are the messages.

c022-p_mwanasiti/dd7bef2b.speaker: c022-p_mwanasiti
c022-p_mwanasiti/dd7bef2b.text: We sold the same fish to the same hotels. That is all.

c022-p_mwanasiti/c65ee7dc.speaker: c022-p_mwanasiti
c022-p_mwanasiti/c65ee7dc.text: Two of us sign M.M. Ask Mariamu.

c022-p_mwanasiti/b299894c.speaker: c022-p_mwanasiti
c022-p_mwanasiti/b299894c.text: Boda boys. Every one of them says he remembers you.

c022-p_mwanasiti/8db347bb.speaker: c022-p_mwanasiti
c022-p_mwanasiti/8db347bb.text: I crossed on the 06:40 ferry like every morning. I was at the old port by seven.

c022-p_mwanasiti/920853d6.speaker: c022-p_mwanasiti
c022-p_mwanasiti/920853d6.text: I didn't speak to Agnes today.

c022-p_mwanasiti/b5fd91c9.speaker: c022-p_mwanasiti
c022-p_mwanasiti/b5fd91c9.text: I went to the cold store. I told her to stop. We shouted. Then I left for the ferry. She was alive. She was laughing at me.

c022-p_mwanasiti/400c7ab9.speaker: c022-p_mwanasiti
c022-p_mwanasiti/400c7ab9.text: I called her. I wanted her to stop. Ask my husband who he sends money to every month. Ask him.

c022-p_thomas/9566f6bf.speaker: c022-p_thomas
c022-p_thomas/9566f6bf.text: Agnes? What do you mean, Agnes?

c022-p_thomas/50ccaa6f.speaker: c022-p_thomas
c022-p_thomas/50ccaa6f.text: The fees. Yes, we shouted. It's been a year of shouting. But she is my children's mother.

c022-p_thomas/37f75867.speaker: c022-p_thomas
c022-p_thomas/37f75867.text: I was on night shift in Nyali.

c022-p_mariamu/4c805ec6.speaker: c022-p_mariamu
c022-p_mariamu/4c805ec6.text: I have nothing to do with that cold store this morning.

c022-p_mariamu/130cb2cb.speaker: c022-p_mariamu
c022-p_mariamu/130cb2cb.text: Mwanasiti signs M.M. too. Since last week she's been like a ghost. Something happened at home.

c022-p_mariamu/71bb03b1.speaker: c022-p_mariamu
c022-p_mariamu/71bb03b1.text: That M.M. isn't me. I was in town by half past six.

c022-p_omari/58eac635.speaker: c022-p_omari
c022-p_omari/58eac635.text: A year. I sent her money every month. My wife found the messages last week. Since then she hasn't said one word to me.

c022-p_zaituni/0f193117.speaker: c022-p_zaituni
c022-p_zaituni/0f193117.text: I was gone forty-five minutes. Forty-five minutes.

c022-p_zaituni/13a50327.speaker: c022-p_zaituni
c022-p_zaituni/13a50327.text: Six blocks. The factory is slow in the morning. I came back at twenty-five to eight.

c022-p_zaituni/24353009.speaker: c022-p_zaituni
c022-p_zaituni/24353009.text: The boda boys wait outside every morning. Charo is always there.

c023-p_rahma/889e95c3.speaker: c023-p_rahma
c023-p_rahma/889e95c3.text: I was here. I was here all afternoon.

c023-p_rahma/4ab35d08.speaker: c023-p_rahma
c023-p_rahma/4ab35d08.text: Auntie Yasmin? She comes sometimes. They argue about the building. In Gujarati, so I don't understand.

c023-p_rahma/dfbb9d06.speaker: c023-p_rahma
c023-p_rahma/dfbb9d06.text: I was in the shop all afternoon. Nobody came.

c023-p_rahma/6198c61b.speaker: c023-p_rahma
c023-p_rahma/6198c61b.text: I went for an interview. A hotel in Nyali. Mama didn't know. I left the sign. I only wanted a job with a pension. I'm so sorry. I'm so sorry.

c023-p_yasmin/5ad9bd77.speaker: c023-p_yasmin
c023-p_yasmin/5ad9bd77.text: I have heard. I am in mourning. What do you want?

c023-p_yasmin/b8779e87.speaker: c023-p_yasmin
c023-p_yasmin/b8779e87.text: Half mine. Forty million, and she wanted to sit on it selling cloves.

c023-p_yasmin/c0cc275f.speaker: c023-p_yasmin
c023-p_yasmin/c0cc275f.text: Silence. She looks at the rack for a long time and says nothing at all.

c023-p_yasmin/deca666c.speaker: c023-p_yasmin
c023-p_yasmin/deca666c.text: That building is half mine. She was sentimental.

c023-p_ken/0c4ef350.speaker: c023-p_ken
c023-p_ken/0c4ef350.text: Mrs Karimjee? I'm very sorry. What does this have to do with me?

c023-p_ken/aa6189b0.speaker: c023-p_ken
c023-p_ken/aa6189b0.text: One way or another, I said. I meant the courts. Developers sue. We don't kill people.

c023-p_ken/1af6c25b.speaker: c023-p_ken
c023-p_ken/1af6c25b.text: I was presenting at the county planning office.

c023-p_imran/3bf26d63.speaker: c023-p_imran
c023-p_imran/3bf26d63.text: Mummy refused every offer. Auntie Yasmin needs money, everyone knows. But she never had any share of the shop. Only the building.

c023-p_kitsao/6a751b2c.speaker: c023-p_kitsao
c023-p_kitsao/6a751b2c.text: Two fares from that number? Yes. The lady in white.

c023-p_hussein/e8e373a1.speaker: c023-p_hussein
c023-p_hussein/e8e373a1.text: Thirty years I carve doors on this pavement. I see every door on Ndia Kuu.

c023-p_hussein/e155dda0.speaker: c023-p_hussein
c023-p_hussein/e155dda0.text: The girl put a sign up and went off at twenty-five to four, in her best clothes. I thought: a boy.

c024-p_ireri/b00833ed.speaker: c024-p_ireri
c024-p_ireri/b00833ed.text: Terrible. Terrible. Khamis was a legend on this water.

c024-p_ireri/7742d1d4.speaker: c024-p_ireri
c024-p_ireri/7742d1d4.text: A fair offer. Twice. He liked to say no. Old men like to say no.

c024-p_ireri/2d6449c5.speaker: c024-p_ireri
c024-p_ireri/2d6449c5.text: He took them off to swim. He did that. Everyone knows.

c024-p_ireri/90f823fb.speaker: c024-p_ireri
c024-p_ireri/90f823fb.text: His crewman stole fuel and got sacked last week. Ask him where he was.

c024-p_ireri/6bb8e77a.speaker: c024-p_ireri
c024-p_ireri/6bb8e77a.text: I haven't been to the old harbour since Sunday. I was home in Kisauni all night.

c024-p_ireri/7e9956ff.speaker: c024-p_ireri
c024-p_ireri/7e9956ff.text: Khamis and I were friends. I chartered his dhow.

c024-p_ireri/143cc7da.speaker: c024-p_ireri
c024-p_ireri/143cc7da.text: I rowed out at midnight. All right. I made him a fair offer, the last one. He said no again, like always. I rowed back. He was alive. He was laughing at me.

c024-p_swaleh/0a0fb656.speaker: c024-p_swaleh
c024-p_swaleh/0a0fb656.text: I did wrong. I know. But I didn't do this.

c024-p_swaleh/b08a7ed1.speaker: c024-p_swaleh
c024-p_swaleh/b08a7ed1.text: I took fuel. Mzee gave me a second chance three times. The fourth time he was right.

c024-p_swaleh/0071bdea.speaker: c024-p_swaleh
c024-p_swaleh/0071bdea.text: People say Mzee reported the cruise man for smuggling. I don't know. People say many things.

c024-p_swaleh/acc35739.speaker: c024-p_swaleh
c024-p_swaleh/acc35739.text: I was on night watch at Marikiti.

c024-p_abdalla/37118ed4.speaker: c024-p_abdalla
c024-p_abdalla/37118ed4.text: Baba is dead. They are saying he went fishing alone.

c024-p_abdalla/982e1eef.speaker: c024-p_abdalla
c024-p_abdalla/982e1eef.text: I got that at two in the morning and I was afraid. Baba never sent an SMS in his life. He can't read. He calls.

c024-p_abdalla/3b9e9f55.speaker: c024-p_abdalla
c024-p_abdalla/3b9e9f55.text: I wrote HAPANA on it for him. He said, "Write it twice, so they understand.

c024-p_abdalla/e686cacf.speaker: c024-p_abdalla
c024-p_abdalla/e686cacf.text: Ask the Lamu harbour office. My boat was here all night.

c024-p_abdalla/d7152d76.speaker: c024-p_abdalla
c024-p_abdalla/d7152d76.text: I was in Lamu. Ask the harbour office there.

c024-p_fumo/3acaa582.speaker: c024-p_fumo
c024-p_fumo/3acaa582.text: Thirty years he moored beside me. He swam like a fish. He did not drown.

c024-p_fumo/f0e5435f.speaker: c024-p_fumo
c024-p_fumo/f0e5435f.text: Khamis never took his sandals off on deck. Never. His feet were too old for that wood.

c024-p_hamza/274b7abc.speaker: c024-p_hamza
c024-p_hamza/274b7abc.text: The fishermen said drowning. I wrote drowning.

c024-p_hamza/277aa62e.speaker: c024-p_hamza
c024-p_hamza/277aa62e.text: I came on duty at quarter to six. I didn't see him in the water. I took their word.

c025-p_mwanaidi/4ef06bbf.speaker: c025-p_mwanaidi
c025-p_mwanaidi/4ef06bbf.text: Wrong number? It happens. I sent it back.

c025-p_mwanaidi/59af9157.speaker: c025-p_mwanaidi
c025-p_mwanaidi/59af9157.text: People mistype every day. It's not my fault what people type.

c025-p_mwanaidi/e4c95ca5.speaker: c025-p_mwanaidi
c025-p_mwanaidi/e4c95ca5.text: That money came by mistake and I sent it straight back.

c025-p_mwanaidi/4f512a92.speaker: c025-p_mwanaidi
c025-p_mwanaidi/4f512a92.text: I don't go to Kongowea. I sell phones at Mwembe Tayari. I've never met her.

c025-p_mwanaidi/58307d19.speaker: c025-p_mwanaidi
c025-p_mwanaidi/58307d19.text: I needed it. My mother is in hospital, they want forty thousand before they operate. Eighty-five thousand just arrived. Like God sent it. I took it out before I could think.

c025-p_mwanaidi/80da0789.speaker: c025-p_mwanaidi
c025-p_mwanaidi/80da0789.text: I went to tell her I'd pay it back. Slowly. She shouted. She grabbed my pouch. I pulled away and I left. That's all. That's all.

c025-p_benard/76c68802.speaker: c025-p_benard
c025-p_benard/76c68802.text: Everlyne? Dead? I shouted at her yesterday.

c025-p_benard/0a31d2cb.speaker: c025-p_benard
c025-p_benard/0a31d2cb.text: No money, no more tomatoes, I told her. She swore she'd sent it to the wrong number. I thought she was lying. God forgive me.

c025-p_benard/c96a6816.speaker: c025-p_benard
c025-p_benard/c96a6816.text: I was on the road back to Taveta.

c025-p_linet/b719d764.speaker: c025-p_linet
c025-p_linet/b719d764.text: I am number forty-one and they are serving thirty-six. What is it?

c025-p_linet/5952efa9.speaker: c025-p_linet
c025-p_linet/5952efa9.text: We were splitting up the business. Politely. Accountants, not shouting.

c025-p_linet/3bf05176.speaker: c025-p_linet
c025-p_linet/3bf05176.text: Benard threatened her yesterday. No money, no more tomatoes. Everyone heard.

c025-p_saidi/372a976c.speaker: c025-p_saidi
c025-p_saidi/372a976c.text: I saw them fighting. I didn't think it was serious. People fight here every hour.

c025-p_saidi/2524639a.speaker: c025-p_saidi
c025-p_saidi/2524639a.text: Young. A cap. That pink pouch. Mama Everlyne grabbed it like she wanted to tear it off her.

c025-p_godfrey/730c9122.speaker: c025-p_godfrey
c025-p_godfrey/730c9122.text: Twelve crates at half past ten. She was fine. She was laughing.

c025-p_beatrice/4065bb2f.speaker: c025-p_beatrice
c025-p_beatrice/4065bb2f.text: She told me about the money last night. She was so angry.

c025-p_beatrice/657ea501.speaker: c025-p_beatrice
c025-p_beatrice/657ea501.text: That name was on the message. Everlyne said it over and over last night. Mwanaidi Mwatsahu.

c026-p_rajab/44807268.speaker: c026-p_rajab
c026-p_rajab/44807268.text: Tall. A cap. He ran that way. I saw it all.

c026-p_rajab/3bf6db18.speaker: c026-p_rajab
c026-p_rajab/3bf6db18.text: At about 21:40 I saw a tall man in a cap hit him and run towards Likoni Road.

c026-p_rajab/712b2603.speaker: c026-p_rajab
c026-p_rajab/712b2603.text: I didn't see anything. She called me crying. She gave me three thousand to say it. She said he killed her boy. I have a boy too.

c026-p_felister/135c4b77.speaker: c026-p_felister
c026-p_felister/135c4b77.text: Eight months. Nobody came. Nobody looked. I looked.

c026-p_felister/23819738.speaker: c026-p_felister
c026-p_felister/23819738.text: She hands over the red kanga without being asked. "It's still wet. I washed it last night.

c026-p_felister/43b2db1e.speaker: c026-p_felister
c026-p_felister/43b2db1e.text: A mechanic told me in August. The second of January. A smashed front and a new windscreen, cash, no questions.

c026-p_felister/28a3648c.speaker: c026-p_felister
c026-p_felister/28a3648c.text: He was alive when I got out.

c026-p_said/ad191cf9.speaker: c026-p_said
c026-p_said/ad191cf9.text: My tuk-tuk? What has he done to my tuk-tuk?

c026-p_said/121abffb.speaker: c026-p_said
c026-p_said/121abffb.text: Two weeks behind on the daily rent. Good driver, bad payer.

c026-p_said/63c6c65c.speaker: c026-p_said
c026-p_said/63c6c65c.text: In January he told me he hit a pothole. I believed him. I fixed nothing. He paid himself.

c026-p_said/8cb63602.speaker: c026-p_said
c026-p_said/8cb63602.text: Ask the committee secretary. I sat at that table all evening.

c026-p_said/918cce25.speaker: c026-p_said
c026-p_said/918cce25.text: I was at the football committee.

c026-p_kai/5caadd5b.speaker: c026-p_kai
c026-p_kai/5caadd5b.text: Look. Bamburi. I was in Bamburi.

c026-p_kai/f0bf3eb7.speaker: c026-p_kai
c026-p_kai/f0bf3eb7.text: We fought over the stage. That's the stage. You don't kill a man for the stage.

c026-p_kai/b34482e2.speaker: c026-p_kai
